correctness.rationale: For standard Gaussian surface measure of fixed axis-aligned finite-dimensional orthotope, facet Fubini factorization gives G(t)=C[φ(t-a)+φ(t+a)+Λ(Φ(t+a)-Φ(t-a))] with C=∏q_j and Λ=Σ(2φ(b_j)/q_j), q_j=2Φ(b_j)-1>0. Differentiate: Gʹ(t)=2Cφ(a)e^{-t²/2}cosh(at)[(a-Λ)tanh(at)-t]. If a−Λ≤0 bracket negative for t>0; otherwise its fʹ(0)=δ=a(a−Λ)−1 and fʺ(t)<0 for every t>0. Therefore δ≤0 gives unique centered global max and δ>0 exactly two global maxima ±t*, with t* unique positive root in (0,a−Λ); decay at infinity excludes others. Threshold a_c=(Λ+sqrt(Λ²+4))/2. Taylor expansion of tanh gives t*²=3δ/a_c²+O(δ²), positive gain 3Cφ(a_c)δ²/(2a_c²)+O(δ³), and critical negative quartic coefficient −Cφ(a_c)a_c²/6. Independently checked direct numerical derivative and local phase for multiple widths/dimensions.

value.rationale: An exact all-dimensional translation phase diagram for a standard Gaussian geometric functional on a natural rigid family. It identifies when central symmetry of shape fails to produce centered perimeter maximizers, gives a sharp transverse-width threshold, uniqueness, square-root bifurcation and quartic critical flatness. Unlike broad order-of-magnitude maxima over arbitrary convex sets, this is a precise, motivated extremal classification.

limitations: Fixed orthotope translated only along one coordinate, d>=2; no simultaneous translations, rotations, general convex bodies or arbitrary radial densities.
Unindexed one-variable Gaussian tail extremum classifications may contain an older equivalent.
